description: We’re a team of engineers and problem-solvers passionate about AI/ML, space technology, GIS, data science, and building real-world solutions. We’re looking for curious builders who want to create something ambitious for NASA Space Apps—not just another hackathon project. Skills in AI/ML, Python, GIS, astronomy, UI/UX, data visualization, research, or storytelling are welcome. Let’s build something impactful together!
summary:
FIRELINE (Fire Intelligence & Research Evidence Linkage Engine) is an evidence-first research platform developed for NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge. It transforms a curated subset of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity-combustion records, primarily from Saffire-I and BASS-II, into searchable, source-linked scientific evidence.

Researchers can explore experimental records, evaluate whether different experiments are physically comparable, and assess evidence coverage for ISS, Artemis and Mars mission scenarios. Its SI Copilot retrieves relevant records and audited findings, distinguishing between SUPPORTED, INFERRED and EVIDENCE GAP conclusions, with citation validation and a deterministic fallback.

FIRELINE preserves experimental conditions, measurement units, uncertainty and source provenance. FLEX liquid-droplet combustion research is kept distinct from solid-fuel experiments.

By helping researchers understand what existing evidence supports and where further investigation is needed, FIRELINE aims to improve scientific decision support for future human space exploration. It is a research-support tool, not a fire-risk predictor or certified safety system.
details:
Overview

FIRELINE is an interactive scientific evidence intelligence platform designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research more accessible, comparable and useful for future space exploration.

For decades, NASA has conducted combustion experiments in microgravity. However, research findings are distributed across scientific publications, experimental tables, engineering records and supporting datasets. Comparing results without considering their physical conditions can lead to scientifically invalid conclusions.

FIRELINE addresses this problem through an evidence-first research workflow.

How It Works

  1. DATA INGESTION: FIRELINE processes NASA PSI experimental records from Saffire-I and BASS-II using a Python-based ingestion pipeline.
  2. SCIENTIFIC VALIDATION: Pydantic contracts and deterministic validation rules preserve original units, experimental conditions, uncertainty and provenance. Missing measurements remain null rather than being fabricated.
  3. EVIDENCE EXPLORATION: Researchers search, filter and inspect experimental records through an interactive Next.js dashboard.
  4. PHYSICAL COMPARABILITY: A deterministic multi-criteria engine evaluates experimental regime, fuel material, geometry, airflow, pressure, oxygen concentration and burn orientation before allowing meaningful comparisons.
  5. MISSION ASSESSMENT: Researchers evaluate ISS, Artemis and Mars environmental scenarios against the available experimental evidence to identify uncharacterized conditions.
  6. SI COPILOT: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines keyword-based evidence retrieval, audited scientific findings and Google Gemini integration. Citation validation checks generated references, with a deterministic fallback when the AI provider is unavailable or a response fails validation.

FIRELINE classifies findings as SUPPORTED, INFERRED or EVIDENCE GAP.

Technology Stack

Frontend: Next.js 15, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.

Backend and Processing: Python 3.12, Pydantic 2 and Next.js API routes.

Data: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), structured JSON evidence records and Supabase/PostgreSQL schema migrations.

AI: Google Gemini API, retrieval-based evidence synthesis and citation validation.

Visualization: Three.js.

Testing and Deployment: Pytest, TypeScript, ESLint, GitHub and Render.

Algorithms and Scientific Approach

FIRELINE primarily uses deterministic, rule-based scientific validation rather than a trained machine-learning fire-prediction model.

Its main algorithmic components include:

  • Multi-criteria physical comparability gates.
  • Deterministic boundary and parameter validation.
  • Keyword-based evidence relevance ranking.
  • Rule-based mission evidence-gap assessment.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
  • Automated citation validation and deterministic fallback.

The platform does not generate fire-risk probabilities or certify spacecraft safety.

Creativity and Innovation

FIRELINE's central innovation is its emphasis on scientific comparability and epistemic transparency.

Instead of treating every matching research result as interchangeable, it evaluates physical conditions before drawing comparisons. It also makes uncertainty explicit and identifies where available evidence is insufficient.

FLEX liquid-droplet combustion findings are kept separate from solid-fuel experimental records to prevent invalid cross-phase comparisons.

Benefits and Intended Impact

FIRELINE helps combustion researchers, aerospace engineers, materials scientists and mission planners discover relevant experimental evidence more efficiently.

Its long-term goal is to support better-informed research and identify experiments needed to address evidence gaps for future lunar habitats and Mars missions.

FIRELINE is intended as scientific decision support for qualified experts, not a replacement for engineering certification or official spacecraft fire-safety procedures.
